title: Prana indicator rule set
description: One versioned, citable rule set, stored at rules/<area>/<id>.json. Every indicator the app shows names the rule set and version that produced it, so a number on the screen can be traced to a published document. Rule sets hold transcribed thresholds and never a health verdict: they decide whether a value is higher or lower than a published reference, not whether a food is good.

version.description: Semantic version of this rule set, shown to the user beside the rule name. Raise the major version when a threshold changes, because that changes what people were told.

title.description: Short name shown when an indicator is tapped.

kind.description: nutrient_bands places a value in a Lower/Moderate/Higher band from fixed published cut-offs. category_limits compares against a published per-category limit and reports above or below it. peer_comparison ranks a value against other products in the same category in this catalogue.

summary.description: Plain English, shown in the explanation sheet. Say what the rule compares and against what. No health claim, no advice.

applies_to.description: Which nutrition panels this rule set may be used on. A rule set written for solid food per 100 g must never be applied to a drink per 100 ml.

basis.description: The basis the thresholds are expressed in.

form.description: Published thresholds differ between solid foods and drinks, so the form is part of the rule set rather than guessed at.

source.description: Where these numbers were transcribed from. Required, and it is the point of the whole format: a threshold without a citation is an invented number.

published.description: Year or date of the edition transcribed, as printed on it.

licence.description: The licence the source document is published under, which decides whether we may reproduce its numbers.

locator.description: Where in the document the numbers are, for example "Annex 3, Table 2". Lets a reviewer check a transcription without reading the whole thing.

notes.description: Anything a reviewer needs in order to judge whether the transcription is faithful, including what the source does not cover.

bands.description: For kind nutrient_bands. One entry per nutrient the rule set can place in a band.

limits.description: For kind category_limits. One entry per category the source publishes a limit for.

NutrientUnit.description: Units nutrients are declared in. Deliberately not the shared Unit enum, which describes package sizes and has no milligrams.

Nutrient.description: salt_g is not stored on any record. It exists because published thresholds are commonly expressed as salt while labels declare sodium, and a rule that needs it must say so through derived_from rather than have the conversion buried in code.

Derivation.description: How to obtain a nutrient that records do not carry, from one they do. Declared here rather than in code so that a reviewer can see every arithmetic step between the label and the screen.

multiply_by.description: Factor applied to the stored value, including any unit change.

note.description: Why this factor is correct. A fixed chemical ratio is acceptable here; an estimate is not.

Band.description: Cut-offs placing one nutrient in Lower, Moderate or Higher. Boundaries follow the source exactly: at or below lower_at_or_below is Lower, above higher_above is Higher, and everything between is Moderate.

portion_higher_above.description: Some sources add a second Higher test against the amount in one portion, which catches a modest concentration in a large serving.

portion_applies_above.description: The portion test applies only when the portion exceeds this size, in the unit of applies_to.basis.

CategoryLimit.description: A published limit for one Prana category. category_id is ours; source_category records what the source calls it, so a reviewer can check the mapping, which is the step most likely to be wrong.

above.description: The published limit. A value above it is reported as above the limit, and nothing more than that is claimed.

PeerComparison.description: Ranks a value against other products in the same category in this catalogue. This is the only rule kind whose output depends on our own data, so it carries a minimum peer count: below it, the comparison is not shown at all rather than shown weakly.

minimum_peers.description: Below this many peers with a comparable value, no comparison is offered.
